subject: Gateway Labs — inference cost snapshot & pilot path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@gatewaylabs.com>, Gateway Labs Technical <eng@gatewaylabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Gateway Labs — inference cost snapshot & pilot path

Alicia / Gateway team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to align. TL;DR: we heard high token spend driven by per-transaction authorization prompts + long fraud context windows; target is to get cost per transaction down ~35–45% while preserving detection quality and staying within a ~$12k–15k monthly inference budget for the pilot.

Pain points we captured:
- Each transaction generates ~4 model calls (auth prompt, risk-score, rerank, explanation) — ~1.2k tokens total on average.
- Peak windows (taxi-burst style) cause lots of small single-request spikes — batching not currently used.
- Fraud models need 2–4k token context for complete session history which inflates cost.
- Procurement wants a clear TCO and an initial cap for the POC.

Goals you stated:
- Reduce per-transaction inference cost by ~40% (without >1.5% delta in false positives).
- Keep 95th percentile latency under ~120ms for real-time auth path (can tolerate slightly higher for async rerank).
- Run a 4–6 week pilot on production-ish traffic (50–100k txns / month).

Cost/TCO levers we recommend (high level):
1) Batching + micro-window aggregation — group quick auth calls during 1–3s micro-windows to amortize KV/cache warmup and tokens. Expect 20–35% token-cost reduction on auth path depending on traffic burstiness.
2) Prefix / KV caching for static prompt sections — common customer/merchant metadata can be cached; reduces repeated tokenization and lowers compute.
3) Context truncation + smart retrieval — move long session history into a lightweight retrieval layer and only surface top-k segments to the model (trade small quality delta for big token savings).
4) Model variant + quantization plan — start hosted with a cost-optimized open model; if quality holds, move to a quantized dedicated variant in Dedicated/Private for 10–25% further unit-cost wins.

Proposed pilot scope (what success looks like):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2 weeks baseline + 4 weeks experiment)
- Metrics: tokens/txn, cost per 1k reqs, p95 latency, fraud detection delta (FP/FN), cache hit rate, throughput.
- Controls: A/B split traffic (10–20% shadow/10% live) or canary routing with fallback.

Attachments I dropped for your review: Gateway_Usage_Snapshot.csv (sample traffic), redwood_pilot_proposal_v1.pdf (timelines & responsibilities).

Next steps I suggest: 
- You confirm pilot budget ceiling (you mentioned ~$12k but procurement said they might allow up to $15k this quarter).
- Gateway shares a 3–7 day sample of anonymized request logs and a minimal test dataset for quality checks.
- We schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff this week to scope batching windows and the retrieval interface.

Proposed meeting slots: Wed 6/16 9–10am PT, Thu 6/17 11–12pm PT, Fri 6/18 2–3pm PT.

Happy to adjust — I can also run a quick ballpark TCO table for two scenarios (no batching vs batching+cache) and put numbers behind the tradeoffs before procurement signs off.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Gateway_Usage_Snapshot.csv (csv, 46KB)]
[Attachment: redwood_pilot_proposal_v1.pdf (pdf, 210KB)]

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@gatewaylabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Gateway Labs Technical <eng@gatewaylabs.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway Labs — inference cost snapshot & pilot path

Ben — really helpful write-up, thanks. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget: procurement is targeting a hard cap of $15k for the POC this quarter (they asked that anything beyond requires exec approval). So please show a scenario that fits under that.
2) PCI / data handling: our security team flagged that any hosted solution that touches cardholder data must be scoped carefully. For the auth path we can send tokenized/no-card payloads to a hosted endpoint, but anything with raw PAN must run in Private/Dedicated. I attached our PCI-compliance-checklist to the thread.
3) Traffic sample: we'll share 7 days of sanitized logs by EOD tomorrow; look for a shared link from eng@gatewaylabs.com.
4) Timeline: procurement prefers decisions by EOW 6/18 so they can include it in the monthly spend plan.

We'd like the TCO scenarios (no batching vs batching + cache) with per-month cost and expected detection impact. Also include any one-time integration effort estimate (hours). If you can send that before EOD 6/16 that would be ideal.

I'll take Wed 6/16 9am PT for the kickoff. Please calendar invite and include any pre-reads.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product Operations, Gateway Labs
[Attachment: PCI-compliance-checklist.pdf (pdf, 78KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@gatewaylabs.com>, Gateway Labs Technical <eng@gatewaylabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway Labs — inference cost snapshot & pilot path

Alicia — thanks, great context. Confirmed: Wed 6/16 9am PT for the kickoff (invite sent).

Attached is a quick ballpark TCO file (ballpark_tco_scenarios.xlsx) — highlights below (high level, back-of-envelope):
- Scenario A (no batching, hosted): ~$14.8k/mo for 75k txns (1.2k tokens/txn average) — gives baseline latency but higher unit cost.
- Scenario B (batching + prefix caching, hosted): ~$9.6k/mo for same traffic — ~35% reduction in token units, modest infra overhead to batch windows. Expected detection delta: ~0.5% nit (can be validated by quality holdout).
- Scenario C (batching + cache + quantized dedicated): ~$7.8k/mo steady-state (after moving to Dedicated with quantized model) — requires a 6–8 week migration and minimum committed capacity.

One-time integration effort: ~40–80 engineer hours for batching hooks + retrieval adapter + monitoring (range depends on how much of your pipeline we can reuse).

Given the $15k cap, Scenario B fits well as a short-term pilot. We'll clearly separate any flows that touch sensitive data and can run auth on tokenized payloads in hosted while keeping PAN-sensitive flows in your Private environment behind a dedicated model if you prefer.

Next steps I will action this afternoon:
- Finalize the TCO spreadsheet and add an explicit per-week burn rate (will post to the Drive link).
- Share a short pre-read describing the batching approach + safety fallback.
- Rishi to own the technical kickoff and run a quick perf projection based on your 7-day log.

If procurement needs any wording for the SOW/PO, loop me in and I can provide a one-paragraph commercial summary they can attach.

Regards,
Ben
[Attachment: ballpark_tco_scenarios.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)]
